title: Low-voltage wiring and the certificate
why: We size the cables, earth the install, fit the protection, and issue the certificate of compliance against this before handover.

title: PV and battery on a building supply
why: We wire the rooftop PV or hybrid inverter as part of the building supply and sign it off with the low-voltage certificate.

title: Medium-voltage site intake
why: On a site with a medium-voltage intake or transformer we do not use the low-voltage board rules on that side.

title: Grid connection of the inverter
why: We do not commission a grid-tied inverter until the utility has accepted the connection.

title: Small low-voltage grid connection
why: Before we order the inverter we confirm with the municipality or Eskom whether this site uses the simplified connection or the full one.

title: Supply voltage quality
why: When a site reports dips or flicker we describe them in the utility's terms, and we do not set our own limits.

title: PV test sheets and handover pack
why: We fill in the inspection sheets and the system record on site and hand them over with the job.

title: PV string wiring and DC isolation
why: We set the string layout, the DC cable and the isolation before the modules go down.

title: Module type approval
why: We check the module datasheet for this qualification before we buy modules.

title: Module safety approval
why: We ask for the module safety certificate as well as the type approval before we place the order.

title: PV wiring inside the building
why: We install the PV supply so it meets the building wiring rules, not as a separate system with its own habits.

title: Earthing and shock protection
why: Bond PV frames and battery and inverter cases to earth and fit the right earth leakage, because a bad earth can leave metal live without tripping.

title: Inverter safety listing
why: We do not install a PV inverter that has no safety listing to this standard.

title: Inverter stops when the grid drops
why: We leave anti-islanding on and we open the grid breaker to confirm the inverter stops.

title: Lithium cell safety
why: We look for this safety standard on the battery datasheet before we accept the pack.

title: Battery room and cabinet safety
why: We include ventilation, access and isolation of the battery room or cabinet in the install.

title: Battery system safety
why: We treat the battery, inverter and protection as one storage system, not a loose pack of cells.

title: Listed battery cabinet
why: If a cabinet claims a UL listing we check that the listing covers the whole system, not only a cell inside it.

title: Battery fire spread test
why: When we set battery spacing or the room layout we use the fire-spread test report, not a guessed clearance.

title: Where the battery may sit
why: We use it as a checklist for battery location and fire access, and we still sign the wiring to SANS 10142-1.

title: Inverter grid settings
why: Inverter menus use these names, but the settings we leave on site still have to match NRS 097 and the local utility.

title: UPS performance
why: We check whether the client asked for a UPS or a battery inverter, because an off-grid inverter is not a UPS.

title: Genset rating and duty
why: We read the genset rating and duty on the nameplate before we use it in the changeover or the PLC.

title: Motor and generator ratings
why: When we start or protect a motor or generator we take the rating and the duty from the machine data.

title: Breakers, contactors and isolators
why: We use each device only for the current, voltage and duty on its label, and we do not put an AC device on a DC string.

title: Built switchboard
why: A board we design and populate is checked as a complete assembly, not only as a box of listed parts.

title: Enclosure dust and water rating
why: For an outdoor inverter or roof box we read both IP digits and match them to the site.

title: Surge protection
why: We fit surge protection on the PV DC side and the AC side, and we bond it.

title: Lightning protection
why: A roof with modules, frames and DC cable gets a lightning protection design, because the array frame alone is not that design.

title: Explosive areas
why: If a battery room, fuel store or genset area is a hazardous zone we do not put ordinary electrical gear in it.

title: Electrical noise on controls
why: When a PLC resets next to a drive or inverter we fix the cable route, screen and earth before we change the program.

title: Converter and drive safety
why: For a storage converter or a drive we ask which safety standard the box was built to.

title: Substation data points
why: If a protection relay or grid meter uses IEC 61850 we get its point list, because a Modbus map does not describe it.

title: Utility remote control link
why: We do not offer the municipality this link unless we have the protocol and an agreed point list.

title: What the PLC standards cover
why: We use this to see which PLC standard applies, then we use the hardware and language parts for the actual work.

title: PLC hardware rating
why: We check the temperature and supply rating of a PLC or remote I/O before we put it in a hot outdoor panel.

title: PLC program languages
why: We write structured text in PC Worx and PLCnext with signal names the next person can follow.

title: PLC network security
why: We change default passwords, we close unused remote access, and we keep the PLC off the site guest network.

title: RS-485 wiring
why: We wire Modbus RTU as one daisy chain, terminate both ends, and earth the shield at one point only.

title: Modbus register map
why: We take the register map and the scaling from that device's manual, not from a generic list.

title: Building energy target
why: If the building has an energy target we check it with the architect before we size the PV or the storage.

title: Building energy rules
why: Hot water, lighting and the building shell stay with this document, and our plant does not replace them.

title: Lock-out and the certificate
why: We lock out and prove the circuit is dead, and we do not sign a certificate for work we did not inspect.

title: Generation licence or registration
why: We ask which NERSA approval this plant needs before we run it in parallel with the grid.

title: Modbus word order
why: We check one known value, such as a voltage we can measure, before we trust a 32-bit value split across two registers.

title: Register scaling
why: We apply the scale from the device manual in one place in the PLC program, then we check it with a meter.

title: Cold string voltage
why: We size each string so the open-circuit voltage on a cold morning stays inside the inverter's maximum DC voltage.

title: Anti-islanding
why: We open the grid-side breaker and confirm the inverter stops, because a setting on the screen is not that test.

title: Charge versus battery health
why: We do not tell the client the battery is healthy because the state of charge reads full.

title: Battery charge rate
why: We stay inside the charge and discharge rates the manufacturer publishes for that battery.

title: Peak shaving
why: We agree the demand ceiling with the client, and the PLC alarms before the site reaches it.

title: Time-of-use charging
why: We put the tariff seasons and time bands in the PLC and we check them against the current municipal tariff.
